Etymology tree
Punic 𐤔𐤏𐤋𐤕 (šʿlt)
Latin Sala Coloniabor.
Arabic سلا
Borrowed from Latin Sala Colonia, from Punic 𐤔𐤏𐤋𐤕 (šʿlt).

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: سَلَا • (salā) I (non-past يَسْلُو (yaslū), verbal noun سَلْو (salw) or سُلُوّ (suluww) or سُلْوَان (sulwān))
g: to forget, to think no more of

kaikki_vikisozluk.e:
سلا (form I)
# سَلَّا (sallā) /sal.laː/: third-person masculine dual past active of سَلَّ (salla)
# سُلَّا (sullā) /sul.laː/:
## third-person masculine dual past passive of سَلَّ (salla) and سُلَّ (sulla)
## second-person dual imperative of سَلَّ (salla)
تَسَلَّى • (tasallā) V (non-past يَتَسَلَّى (yatasallā), verbal noun تَسَلٍّ (tasallin))
g: to be amused, to be entertained
to be solaced, to be assuaged, to be comforted

kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Derived from the active participle of سَلَّى (sallā, “to comfort, to amuse”), from the roots س ل و (s l w) and س ل ي (s l y).
